title: Signal prototyping checklist & dashboard sandbox notes
content:
Purpose:

This is a lightweight working doc for signal prototyping: fast experiments to validate whether a metric or trace anchor gives useful, actionable signal for operators and devs. Aim is to keep prototyping cheap (low qps sampling, short retention, small dashboard slices) and then promote to canonical metric with contracts if useful.

Scope / Intended use:
- Short-lived experiments run by eng + product to answer: does this metric detect regressions, provide reliable attribution, and stay within query/cost budgets?
- Focus areas: KV cache / prefix-caching effects, batching behavior, model-routing heat (fallbacks), and perceived vs. raw latency for token-serving paths.
- Not a canonical metric catalog. If an experiment succeeds, follow the metric lifecycle doc to harden.

Quick heuristics (operational):
- Keep sampling <= 1% for noisy token-level traces during prototyping.
- Start with 7d retention, increase only if signal is clearly valuable.
- Prioritize metrics that narrow investigation time (reduce MTTR) over purely statistical coverage.
- Cost guardrail: any new high-cardinality metric needs explicit approval from telemetry-steering; add a low-cardinality rollup first.

Candidate metrics to prototype (short descriptions + what success looks like):

1) per-route median cold-start-latency-ms
- Definition: median latency for requests where prefix-KV cache miss and cold KV warm-up events flagged.
- Why: distinguishes cold-cache from congested infer nodes.
- Success: correlates with error-rate spikes and decreases when cache warmup optimization is applied.

2) kv-cache-hit-streak-length (p50/p90)
- Definition: number of consecutive requests for the same session/tenant that hit prefix cache. Low-cardinality label: tenant_id_hash_8.
- Why: proxy for user-level cache warmth; helps detect tenant-specific cold spills.
- Success: high predictive power for per-tenant token-cost reductions after caching changes.

3) batching-wait-ms (queued-to-dispatch) by model-type
- Definition: time spent in the batching queue before dispatch. Bucketed into sub-ms, ms, tens-ms, 100ms+.
- Why: tuning batching policy or autoscaler when tail latency increases.
- Success: heatmap shows spikes correlated with throughput bursts and cost spikes.

4) fallback-model-rate and fallback-latency
- Definition: percent of requests routed to fallback model variant and their end-to-end latency.
- Why: evaluate the efficacy and cost/latency impact of fallbacks during capacity pressure.
- Success: can set SLOs for fallback latency and reason about user-visible impact.

Tracing anchors & span instrumentation notes:
- Minimal spans to add for experiments: "request.receive", "router.route", "queue.wait", "model.dispatch", "kv.lookup", "kv.update", "response.stream".
- Attach lightweight tags: route_id, model_variant, tenant_bucket, kv_cache_hit (bool), batching_id (uuid prefix).
- Sampling: for early experiments set trace sampling to 0.5% of requests but 100% for traces that hit errors or fallbacks.
- Correlation keys: ensure each span includes request_id and session_id (hashed). Avoid high-card labels like full tenant id unless hashed.

Dashboard sandbox ideas (panels to iterate quickly):
- Incident triage strip: stacked area of requests / errors / 95p latency, with annotation band for cache-cold windows.
- Heatmap: batching-wait-ms over time by model-type (y-axis model, x-axis time, color intensity = p95).
- Scatter: kv-cache-hit-streak-length vs per-request token-cost (sampled points) to see cost correlation.
- Fallback tracer: table of recent fallback traces (sampled) with time-to-first-byte and final-token-latency.
- Cost guardrail widget: token-economics panel (tokens/s, cost-per-token-avg, expected-monthly-USD delta for config change).

Queries / examples (prometheus-style pseudo-expressions for prototyping):
- p50_cold_start_latency_ms = histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{cache_cold="true"}[5m])) by (le, route))
- batching_wait_p95 = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch_wait_bucket[5m])) by (model_variant, le))
- fallback_rate = sum(rate(requests_total{route=~".*", fallback="true"}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m]))

Experiment triage checklist (pre-run):
- [ ] Owner + reviewer assigned (owner = Aisha P.)
- [ ] Hypothesis written: what we expect and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Sampling strategy documented (trace sampling %, metric retention)
- [ ] Query budget estimate posted to telemetry-cost channel
- [ ] Dashboard prototype created with low-cardinality rollups
- [ ] Alert/noise plan: how to mute/kill queries if cost/volume spikes

During experiment (ops):
- Record timestamps of config gates, rollouts, and external events (deployments, infra maintenance).
- Keep a short changelog in the dashboard description so reviewers can map cause/effect.
- If an experiment shows promise after ~48-72 hours, schedule follow-up to harden metric contract.

Promotion checklist (if experiment succeeds):
- Review metric cardinality and add rollups for tenant, region, and model-family.
- Add syntactic metric contract: stable name, units, labels, owner, alert rules, and intended SLOs.
- Move trace sampling for related spans to service-level defaults.
- Add to observability backlog for instrumentation payments (cost allocation).

Query cost & guardrails (practical):
- Each new histogram + per-tenant label multiplies series. When prototyping, prefer aggregated labels and a separate low-cardinality tagged metric for rollups.
- If a query looks expensive in the query profiler, create a derived counter that is cheaper to compute at ingestion time (pre-aggregation).
- Auto-mute policy: any prototyping dashboard generating > $5/day of query spend should be automatically disabled until reviewed. (Tweak threshold as we get real numbers.)

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we allow tenant-level hashed labels by default for all prototyping signals? (privacy vs. triage fidelity)
- What sampling floor do we set for traces that include fallback events? Current recommendation: 100% for fallbacks but cap to 5% total fallback traces if fallback rate spikes.
- Who signs off on adding new high-cardinality histograms? Proposal: telemetry-steering + owning service lead.

Next steps (action items):
- Jonas: spin up dashboard prototype for kv-cache-hit-streak + batching heatmap (due 2024-09-24).
- Evelyn: test trace sampling knobs in staging and report estimated trace storage delta (due 2024-09-30).
- Ravi: draft a short runbook entry for query mutex/kill switch and auto-mute policy (due 2024-10-07).
- Aisha: consolidate experiment into a follow-up PR with acceptance criteria if the metric passes the 72-hour check.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Could try a synthetic probe that warms KV prefix for a tenant sample and then measures hit-streak length as a ground truth.
- Consider a nightly cheap aggregation job that pre-computes per-tenant cache-warmth score to avoid high-cardinality live queries.
- Keep the dashboard UI intentionally minimal: operators should get to an initial hypothesis within 30s of opening.

- Confluence: telemetry-guidelines (placeholder)
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-119 (experiment backlog)
- PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-prs/42

End of sandbox doc.
